newsitem.title: INDIA: India says keeping eye on Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: India says keeping eye on Pakistan.

text.p: India said on Wednesday it was keeping a close watch on neighbouring Pakistan in case any rise in political and economic instability spilled over the border.
Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said political turmoil in Pakistan, which resulted in the recent sacking of prime minister Benazir Bhutto, was an internal affair.
"But it would be incorrect for us to assume that whatever changes take place do not affect the neighbouring countries," Gujral told New Delhi-based Asian News International (ANI).
"They do. So we are keeping a very close watch on what is happening there," he said in an interview
Gujral said instability in Pakistan was becoming "more highlighted" than in the past.
"At the same time, we find the economic situation has a downspin to an extent that they have to import even an expert from the... World Bank to take charge of the ministries," he said.
He was referring to Shahid Javed Burki, a senior World Bank official who took charge of Pakistan's Finance Ministry after Bhutto was sacked and caretaker Meraj Khalid took office.
"Similarly, we also see that they are interested in Afghanistan, the way they have tried to destabilise and contribute to destabilisation of that country further," Gujral said.
Pakistan has denied India's claims that Islamabad backs the Taleban militia, which captured the Afghan capital Kabul in late September.
Gujral said: "Naturally, we keep a watch on them... I'm reacting to and thinking of Pakistan as a neighbouring country in which the elements and symptoms of instability are more than in the past."

India's foreign minister said New Delhi had scored a "victory" by recently holding local elections in Kashmir, where more than 20,000 people have died since a separatist revolt erupted nearly seven years ago.
Pakistan denies India's claims that Islamabad arms and trains guerrillas fighting Indian rule in Kashmir.
Gujral said India had been fighting a "proxy war" in Kashmir.
"That is over and India's victory. Now what is happening is mopping up operation of the victory," he said, referring to raids by Indian security forces against militants.
"So that problem is over so far as we are concerned."
Gujral said it would be unrealistic for Pakistan's caretaker government to take any major initiatives towards India before general elections set for February.
